findings.text: Sysfs name intake rejects empty input and input reaching CS_NAME_LEN, discards one trailing newline when present, transfers normalized bytes to caller storage with termination, and reports original input length on success.
Clocksource removal serializes with registration activity and succeeds immediately for already detached instances, otherwise delegating to shared detach logic while holding the serialization mutex.

Raw fast nanosecond readout offers a non-traced high frequency query that observes the raw fast timekeeper through a retrying latch snapshot combining stored base time with freshly accumulated offset.

Explicit processor timer arming guarantees pinned placement, prior initialization, rejection of duplicate queueing, silent skipping of shutdown instances, atomic migration across bases, base clock advancement, and wheel insertion under the correct base lock.

Timer cancellation reports whether a queued instance was detached, leaves idle instances untouched, and under shutdown also blocks future rearming by clearing the callback while holding the base lock.

Device unbind control maps user supplied naming to a registered event device and releases the addressed processor or broadcast slot, using a fast attempt under list protection with a slower mutex protected retry on contention, returning input size on success.

Clockevents sysfs bringup registers the subsystem, then creates per-processor devices identified by processor number with current binding and unbind controls, plus a broadcast device with current binding control, aborting on first failure; broadcast bringup may compile to an inert success.
Broadcast pseudo device is statically defined with a fixed broadcast name, zero numeric identity, and membership in the clockevents subsystem.

Watchdog test source is statically defined with a fixed test name, low rating of ten, full sixty four bit cycle range, a custom read hook driven by raw time, prelinked list linkage, and flags marking continuity plus calibration plus mandatory verification plus test participation.
Fast time observation retries over alternating latch generations until a consistent generation is seen, summing a stored base with a computed live offset for that generation.

Watchdog test injector supports quiet plus delayed plus forward skewed plus backward skewed base behaviors with an independent high bit selecting remote processor only perturbation, decoded by masking out the high bit for mode choice, where delay stalls about half a millisecond and returns unskewed time.
Test skew sampling refreshes cached interval and attempt count at most once per quarter second of raw time, preserving stability when watchdog reads repeat within one interval.

Global skew alternates between zero and a downshifted cached interval on successive sampling periods, while remote only mode returns zero on the designated watchdog processor and a fixed one millisecond skew elsewhere.

Test mode reset unregisters any prior test source, installs a new base mode with optional remote only decoration, clears sampling history, restores low rating and base flags with optional per processor marking, and re-registers at a nominal one million kilohertz rate.

Unbind holds a sleepable mutex for the whole operation to stabilize the located device, acquiring an irq safe raw list lock only during name lookup and dropping it before any potentially blocking release step.

Clocksource detachment attempts replacement of active roles before removal, refusing with busy status when watchdog or current roles cannot be handed off, tolerating missing suspend replacement, and performing watchdog list removal under irq safe spin protection while outer membership is mutex protected.

Watchdog selection runs atomically under irq safe protection, retaining the previous watchdog when no candidate qualifies or when fallback search finds no alternative, and resetting supervision markings plus ensuring timer activity when identity changes.
Watchdog candidacy requires continuous operation and absence of a self verification requirement, excludes the incumbent during fallback search, and prefers the highest rating among survivors.

Watchdog supervision timer exists only while watched sources remain, starting pinned on the boot processor with a fixed interval on first arrival and stopping when the last watched source leaves, with supervision markings cleared on every watchdog identity change.

Suspend source candidacy requires nonstop behavior across suspend, emits a warning when such a candidate also supplies suspend callbacks, prefers highest rating, and permits the suspend role to remain empty when no replacement exists during removal.

When watchdog supervision is disabled at build time, watchdog identity queries always report absence and selection plus dequeue plus locking operations are inert, while suspend identity stays a pointer comparison and current fallback delegates to generic selection in replacement mode.

Timer base resolution honors pinning for local versus global choice and redirects deferrable timers to a dedicated base when common tickless support is enabled, while cross base moves are marked migrating so concurrent acquirers spin and revalidate flags instead of locking the wrong base.
Base clock movement is monotonic and bounded above by current tick count and by next scheduled horizon, refusing to step past an inconsistent horizon that lies behind the current clock.

Wheel slot choice partitions expiry distance into geometrically spaced levels, rounds placement outward to level granularity so expiry never precedes the requested time, directs already past expiries to the current slot, and clamps excessively distant expiries to wheel capacity.

Wheel insertion records bucket occupancy and the chosen bucket position in flag storage, and when the bucket horizon precedes the base horizon it advances that horizon, marks pending work, clears any recomputation request, and evaluates a remote wake.

Insertion wakeups are fully suppressed when tickless timer activity is disabled or for deferrable timers, otherwise only idle bases cause a remote wake with an expectation of pinned placement or full tickless target.

Timer detachment unlinks bucket membership, clears bucket occupancy only for the final member while requesting horizon recomputation, poisons linkage after unlink, optionally clears pending state, and under shutdown nulls the callback under lock to prevent requeue during or after execution.

Timer hazards comprise duplicate queueing, wrong base locking during migration, rearming across shutdown, and early firing from level truncation, countered by pending checks, migrating spin with flag revalidation, lock protected callback clearing with mandatory locking on shutdown, and outward rounding of bucket horizons.
Unbind lifetime depends on the outer mutex keeping the found device valid after the inner list lock is released and across the slow retry; releasing that mutex early would expose a use after free.
Test skew downshift amount equals eight, realizing an approximately four thousand parts per million perturbation scale.
Remote only modifier for test injection equals two hundred fifty six, occupying a high bit separate from low byte base modes.
Test source flag combination joins continuity with calibration with mandatory verification with test participation, plus an additional per processor test marker when remote only mode is selected.

Wheel geometry uses per level shift equal to level times a base clock shift, per level start equal to level size minus one shifted by predecessor levels, and per level offset equal to level times level size.
Timer objects transition among idle plus queued plus migrating plus shutdown conditions, where migrating blocks base acquisition and shutdown is represented by absent callback with queueing refused.

Timer debug and tickless activity probes compile either to object tracker and branch checks or to inert no operation forms depending on build configuration, covering activation plus deactivation plus initialization assertion plus cancellation tracing.
Watchdog test diagnostics prefix every message with the enclosing module name.
